newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firm on T-bill demand.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firm on T-bill demand.

text.p: The rouble was firm on Wednesday as banks sought funds for today's Treasury bill auction where higher demand is expected after Russia received better than expected credit ratings, dealers said.
They said non-resident demand for T-bills was likely to rise after Russia received a high speculative rating.

Demand for bills is also likely to be strong because today is the last auction with 19 percent effective dollar yield guaranteed by the central bank, they added. As of October 16 the dollar yield will fall to 16 percent.
The central bank is auctioning 10 trillion roubles of six-month bills.

"Demand for T-bills should be huge today. This is why dollar rates are lower and overnight credit rates rose earlier. But at the moment the situation is stable and credit rates have edged down," ABN-Amro Bank chief dealer Dmitry Piskulov said.
He added rouble supply was likely to increase on Thursday as part of the funds which banks failed to invest in T-bills would come back to the rouble/dollar market.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,416-19 per dollar compared with an early 5,422-25 and 5,418-21 late on Tuesday. Tomorrow roubles were steady at 5,424-25 per dollar compared with yesterday's late 5,423-26.
The central bank said it had set 5,420/5,430 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Wednesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 45-60 percent compared with Tuesday's late 40-60 percent.
"Today (dollar) quotes have fallen as banks are selling dollars given high overnight rates," United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said.
"But the central bank is pushing down the rouble and the general trend of its slow, one to two point, decline will remain over the next weeks," he added.
